experiment_name: Horizon diagnostic: does a round-50 net-worth leader predict the round-200 winner, and does the round/max_rounds state encoding alone change model output

part_1_horizon_agreement.opponent_mix: 16 self-play games (model controls all 4 seats) + 16 vs-fixed games (model rotates seats 0-3, 4 times each; fixed-a/b/c fill the other 3 seats)
part_1_horizon_agreement.seed_freshness: self-play 40000-40015, vs-fixed 41000-41015 - no overlap with any prior DEV/eval seed pool in this project (013: self-play 10000-10015, vs-fixed 20000-20015; DDQN paired eval: 10000-10009; 017: 31000-31004; 018: 32000-32009)

part_2_state_encoding_ablation.states_collected: up to 200 non-forced decision states from rounds 1-50 of the same 32 games, deterministic order (game plan order, then turn order), first 200 encountered
part_2_state_encoding_ablation.method: clone the frozen pre-decision game state, flip ONLY env.max_rounds (200 -> 50), verify programmatically that at most one state-vector index changes, then compare POLICY_ONLY model output (chosen action, policy distribution, value head) between the two encodings
part_2_state_encoding_ablation.index_derivation: hand-traced monopoly_game_engine/state.py::build_state_vector's idx arithmetic: state[278] = min(round/max_rounds, 1.0), the only max_rounds-dependent scalar in the 300-dim vector

result: Purely descriptive measurement, no GO/KILL threshold applied (none was pre-registered for this diagnostic - the calling decision is made separately). Part 1: across 32 fresh held-out games at max_rounds=200 (all 32 lived past round 50, so all are in the eligible/agreement sample), the round-50 net-worth leader matched the eventual round-200-or-terminal winner in 19/32 games (59.4% overall) - 6/16 (37.5%) in self-play, 13/16 (81.25%) in vs-fixed. Agreement rose with round-50 margin size (50% at margin <500 and <2000, 68.75% at margin >=2000; mean margin 4061.6 when the round-50 leader went on to win vs. 1590.5 when they didn't), and the round-50 leader ended up ranked 1st at the final tally in 19/32 games, 2nd in 6, 3rd in 5, 4th in 2. Part 2: on the same 200 non-forced rounds-1-50 states, flipping only env.max_rounds (200 vs 50) changed exactly state-vector index 278 in every one of the 200 x 2-checkpoint comparisons (isolation held, verified at runtime, never just assumed) - baseline_pretraining showed 1.5% POLICY_ONLY action disagreement (mean policy TV-distance 0.00237, mean value-head abs delta 0.00136) and trained_updates_500 showed 1.0% action disagreement but a larger policy TV-distance (0.00497) and a roughly 7.5x larger value-head delta (0.01019) than baseline at the identical states - i.e. the 500-update checkpoint's value head is more sensitive to the round/max_rounds encoding alone than the untrained baseline's, even though its final chosen action changes slightly less often. Zero illegal actions, zero crashes, zero ASU modules loaded across the full run.
notes: Full per-game round50_snapshot/final_net_worth/decisions breakdown (32 games) and per-checkpoint ablation aggregates are in the raw stdout log; per-state ablation records (400 = 200 states x 2 checkpoints) are intentionally not persisted anywhere (only their aggregates), consistent with this project's small-raw-stdout convention - each one only ever held small scalars (booleans/floats/an index-count), never the underlying state array. fixed_fallbacks integrity total (90) is entirely from vs-fixed games' non-focus fixed-agent seats (self-play games have none, since no fixed agent is ever seated in a self-play game) - not a fallback by the checkpoint under test itself, which had 0 illegal actions throughout. This experiment makes no GO/KILL call on the 013 replay/training-recipe gate recorded in docs/PLAN.md - it supplies the missing measurement that gate was waiting on; the decision itself is recorded separately once read.
